You’re buying me a **mushroom pizza with caramelized onions, mozzarella, and a little thyme**, plus a **cold, dry apple cider**.

**Why:** Mushrooms bring savory depth, the onions add sweetness, and thyme keeps the whole thing fragrant rather than just rich. The cider’s acidity and bubbles cut through the cheese, while its apple notes complement the onions without competing with the mushrooms.

The guiding principle: **earthy pizza, crisp drink—contrast without a flavor argument.**

You’re buying me a **mushroom, caramelized onion, and goat cheese pizza**, with **sparkling lemonade**.

Why: mushrooms bring earthy savoriness, caramelized onions add sweetness, and goat cheese supplies a tangy contrast—three distinct flavors that complement rather than crowd each other. A thin, crisp crust gives the soft toppings some textural opposition.

The lemonade adds bright acidity against the rich cheese, while the bubbles keep the pairing lively. It’s a meal built around contrast without becoming a chaotic toppings experiment.

You’re buying me a **mushroom pizza with caramelized onions, mozzarella, and thyme**, paired with a **crisp, dry apple cider**.

Why: mushrooms bring savory depth, caramelized onions add sweetness, and thyme keeps the whole thing aromatic rather than just rich. The cider adds acidity and bubbles to cut through the cheese, while its apple notes complement the onions without overwhelming the mushrooms.

The guiding principle: **earthy pizza, bright drink—contrast that still feels coherent.**

You’re buying me a **mushroom pizza with roasted garlic, mozzarella, and a little thyme**, plus a **cold, dry cider**.

Why: mushrooms bring savory depth, roasted garlic adds mellow sweetness, and thyme makes the whole thing aromatic without overpowering it. The cider’s crisp acidity and bubbles would cut through the cheese, while its apple notes would complement the earthy mushrooms. A pairing built on contrast, rather than two things competing to be the loudest.

I’d go for **mushroom, caramelized onion, and goat cheese pizza**, with **a cold, dry apple cider**.

Why: mushrooms bring savory depth, onions add sweetness, and goat cheese supplies tang—three distinct notes rather than one big wall of richness. A slightly charred crust gives it a bitter edge that keeps the sweetness in check.

The cider earns its place because its acidity and bubbles cut through the cheese, while the apple flavor complements the onions. Dry rather than sweet, so the pairing stays crisp instead of turning into dessert.

Basically: earthy pizza, bright drink, good contrast. 🍕
